utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours, this is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and I can understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, please sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, Anna Richterova assisted by Denise Gustin case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you and welcome back, Ms. Gustin. Appearances for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour I'm John Ackerman, here again today with Vesna Anic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we bring in the witness, any particular point that you would like to make or raise? Nothing, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just a very brief announcement, Your Honour, as a result of the meeting yesterday, Ms. Jevtovic will remain for the next two weeks before she departs, so she will be in court for the next two weeks to get us through this period and I appreciate that very much. That will help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for the information, Mr. Ackerman. So let's proceed. Let's bring the witness in. Madam, how long -- how much longer do you think you'll take?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Everybody is asking me. I would like to finish before the first break, which will be 4.00 but it's -- I would like to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And after that, how long do you reckon you need, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour my best guess is that I have about an hour. Maybe a little more. Similar to yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So try to keep it as short as possible, both of you, and stick to the most important, most relevant issues. Is Ms. Korner back or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Not yet. She will be back on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So be prepared, please, Wednesday or Thursday at the latest, we thrash out what's going to happen after the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I'll be ready to report to you on Monday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's great, thank you but we will need to discuss it in any case. Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you follow me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the usher is going to give you again the text of the solemn declaration which I kindly ask you to repeat before you continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Madam Richterova will be continuing with her examination-in-chief. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, before the break yesterday, we were talking among others about the transfer of the TO weapons to Banja Luka. Were you given a reason why these weapons were transferred?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Darko Savic, the manager of Daljan barracks who explained this to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that the JNA had decided that the weapons should be relocated from the Daljan barracks to one of the Banja Luka barracks. So in order to avoid any theft from the barracks, and he also informed me of the fact that the weapons were not safe in the Daljan barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was it a normal procedure, that the JNA would decide how to deal with weapons which belonged to TO?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I reacted to what he had said. I told him that this was not all right, that the weapons were pretty safe in Daljan, and I also offered that it be provided further security by a mixed police group but he nevertheless went to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you say he or that the weapons left for Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons left for Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yesterday, we were also talking about the elections and you said, and it is from your transcript, that the SDA and SDS won. Do you remember which of these two parties won more seats?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA got more seats.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know who was after that elected as the President of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kemal Terzic was elected president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What is his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And who was the President of the municipal executive board?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Zoran Glisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also mentioned that you, in your capacity as the commander of the TO, you attended some of the municipal assembly meetings and you knew the agenda. I would like to show you now a few documents, and if you could make a comment on them? The first one is Exhibit P1702. This document is dated 23rd December, 1991, it was issued by Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Donji Vakuf, and it says, among others, "At the session of the Donji Vakuf municipal assembly, held on 12 December, 1991, the following question was asked by the socialist democratic party board member," and this document is referring to the plebiscite of the Serbian people. Do you know anything about the plebiscite which would take place in the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I knew that a plebiscite was going to be held in Donji Vakuf, and -- well, I was aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were some public meetings where this plebiscite would be discussed?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended several meetings where the plebiscite was not much discussed. The meetings included both the SDS and SDA, but I do not remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And it was the -- this document states that the initiative to separate part of the Donji Vakuf municipality should be raised. Was anything like that discussed? I mean division of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These decisions were usually reached on an interparty basis, on the basis of agreements reached by SDS and SDA. I never attended such interparty meetings. However, within the municipal assembly, I mean I was never invited to attend such meetings or I would be present for a couple of minutes and then would leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show you another document. It's P1703. It is document dated 13 of January, 1992. It's again Serbian Democratic Party, Donji Vakuf, and it says, "The Serbian people of our municipality decided at a plebiscite on 10 November, 1991, to join the SAO Krajina and the following members of the assembly of the SAO Bosanska Krajina would be" -- and now we have the list of seven people. These seven people, these people, were they members of Donji Vakuf municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether all of them were members. But in all likelihood, some of them were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this document is specific about this plebiscite. It took place on 10 November, 1991. Do you know whether all ethnicities participated in this plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And also assembly of SAO Bosanska Krajina is mentioned here. Do you know whether these people participated in any meetings in assembly of the Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know these men personally. I used to know them. And I met with a couple of them even after the conflict. I knew that they attended the assembly, I don't know whether all of them did, but some of them I am sure did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with them or with anybody else their participation in the work of the assembly of the SAO Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Discussions about their participation in some of the institutions of the SAO Krajina were never held. We never talked about those things. But from these conversations, I was able to conclude that they went to Banja Luka occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And at that time, which is January, was the municipal assembly in Donji Vakuf still functioning?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bodies of the municipal assembly in Donji Vakuf were still functioning but I don't think that sessions were convened, sessions of the municipal assembly that would have been attended by the deputies. However, various municipal bodies did work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will show you document P1704. And this document says that based on the will of the Serbian people in Donji Vakuf, expressed in the plebiscite held on 9 and 10 November at its meeting held on 15 February, the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf passed the decision for the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina. It is dated 15 of February, 1992. Did you know that at that time the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf was formed and that this Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf joined the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, because it was not a secret.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was it ever discussed during the assembly meetings, the possibility, first, to establish the Serbian municipality and second to the joint -- to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether such issues were ever discussed, but I know that interparty negotiations were being held, that there was a lot of arguing going on, and I know that the SDS had their own plan on the basis of which they operated, regardless of any agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember that there would be some preparations to create this Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf by collecting some informations?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that one of my employees, my assistant at the TO staff, publicly worked for the Serbian organs, that is for the bodies of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, which were being established at the time, that they were drafting some sort of maps that I was of course able to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You just said drafting some maps, and you saw them. What were these maps about?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those maps were done on the basis of some very old historical maps. The purpose was to delineate accurately Serb land as opposed to the land which belonged to other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown the map which we exhibited yesterday under 1692?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm just going to get the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And at the same time I would like to show the witness Exhibit P1605. And this is the decision on establishment of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, and it says, among others, "These are the area of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf -- or the area of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf shall comprise, A, the local communes, B, settlements, C, parts of inhabited urban and rural local communes." And again the date is 15 of February. My question is: You had the opportunity to have a look at this document. As a person familiar with the distribution of ethnic groups within the municipality, would this proposed division have been practical?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, and I know for a fact, that it would have been impossible to divide the area in this manner. What you have here is actually all of the villages and hamlets of this local community which were inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So would it have allowed normal functioning of divided municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can you -- the reason why I had the map prepared for you, if you could show us the areas with Serb villages, according to this proposal, in interaction with Muslim villages? Because you just said that it couldn't function normally. If you could give us explanation why you think it wouldn't function?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] One moment. Stop, please. Neither Judge Taya nor myself we are not receiving any interpretation in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sir, can I ask to you repeat your answer starting from the beginning, the question was: Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And can you, the reason why I had the map prepared for you, if you could show us the areas with Serb villages according to this proposal and interaction with Muslim villages because you just said that it couldn't function normally, if you could give us an explanation why you think it wouldn't function? And you had started explaining why. Could you repeat what you said, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was saying, it couldn't function because Serbs populated this area, this area, this part here, and this part here, as well as Donji Vakuf. These same parts of the municipality were populated by Muslims as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So was it possible to separate them so both ethnicities had the same facilities, the same access to the town of Donji Vakuf, and main offices?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P1708. It's again a document dated the 15th of February, 1992. It says, "Decision to appoint a president of the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, professor Nikica Zagorac. Did you know that Nikica Zagorac was appointed to the post of president?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I congratulated him on it. I told him, "Aren't you ashamed?" He didn't reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know Nikica Zagorac from before?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew each other very well. We used to work together in high school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was he a teacher?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a teacher of mathematics, and I used to teach defence and protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the last document from this area, and of the same day. It's P1706.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this is -- these are minutes of the constitutional session of the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, held on 15 of February. You said yesterday that your office was in the same building as the municipal -- it was in the building of the -- I'm sorry, you said in the municipal building. Were you aware of this session?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, and I very much doubt that it was held at the municipal assembly at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And on the second page, it says, the proposal was adopted, that the former assemblymen of the Donji Vakuf municipal assembly be appointed -- I'm sorry, for you, it is the same page in original language. All be appointed members of the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf. Did you know whether these 30 or 33 persons were members or formerly appointed, elected municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think some of them were, some weren't. Most of these people I knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, either you already said that you are not aware of this meeting which took place on 15 of February. To your knowledge, were there any meetings of the Serbian municipal assembly which would be held in the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know about any such thing because I doubt very much they were held during working hours. What happened after working hours, I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And after 15 of February, are you aware of any meeting of the other municipal assembly? And when I'm saying "the other," I mean the assembly which was elected in 1991.

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: But were you -- were you ever invited to the meeting or to the meetings of municipal assembly after 15 -- after February 15?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with this document. In your capacity as the commander of the TO, were you -- were you a part of some other official organ within the municipality of Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the council for National Defence for the municipality of Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And who were the members of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the President of the National Defence Council was the President of the municipality. His deputy was president of the executive board at the time, Glisic was his name. Then there was the chief of the police department, otherwise called MUP. He was commander of the municipal staff. Then there was the secretary of the National Defence Secretariat, and the administrator of the Daljan barracks, Darko Samac -- Savic. There may have been other people but I don't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And according to ethnicities, was it a mix or were they just members of one ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you, in 1992, did you attend the meetings of National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you make notes about issues which were discussed at this council?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to go through some notes which the witness made about the events, and so I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1693, which is the diary. And in the diary, I am referring now to the page, translation, 0306-0164, which is page 7, and for the witness, it is page marked by identification number 0207-2300. Can the usher help the witness? In fact, I apologise, it already starts on page 6, for the English translation. It is National Defence Council. It says 10 of February, 1991, but from the notes which follow, it's obvious that it is the year 1992, that it's just a typo, and if you go to the further -- to the next page, in B/C/S, to the page 0207-2301, and on the left-hand side, there is a name Nasmija it says the state of combat readiness in the municipality TO has been impaired. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you make a comment to this note, to this entry?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, we are talking about February, very serious things were happening that disturbed the balance of not only interethnic relations but also the state of combat readiness at the Donji Vakuf TO staff. The very fact that the weaponry was located in Banja Luka, the weaponry of the TO, that is away from Donji Vakuf, meant that the state of combat readiness was not as it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And it goes on as lack of coordination in the work of the parties in power. What did you mean by this entry?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant that one party was working in circumvention of the law, establishing its own municipal organs which had the attribute of Serbian organs, whereas joint organs and agencies, which were supposed to be functioning at the time, were not operating.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said that SDS was creating their own offices and organs. What was the relationship between the SDA and SDS at that time, if you can make any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their relationship was out of kilter. They tried to reach some agreements but even when they succeeded, the SDS never adhered to that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this National Defence Council, the people were members of mostly both these leading parties, and you mentioned that they couldn't make any agreement. Do you remember what kind of proposals were discussed?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often they discussed law enforcement, since armed men were walking about in the streets, wearing Chetnik emblems, emblems of an army which was not our army. Furthermore, they talked about the establishment of joint guards, joint guard posts, joint control of vital facilities in the territory of the Donji Vakuf municipality, and about the establishment of joint checkpoints along thoroughfares, along most important communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You say joint checkpoints. What was the reality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a realistic idea. It was feasible. However, the SDS did not accept this. They did make certain promises but eventually none of these ideas and requests or agreements was ever -- ever came to anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Just quickly talking about these checkpoints, do you know where and when these checkpoints were set up?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was one checkpoint by the so-called Filbar bridge. Another checkpoint was at the exit from Donji Vakuf, in the direction of Bugojno, approximately 200 metres down the road towards Bugojno, counting from the petrol station. And then in February, March and April, a checkpoint was set up more than once on the road towards Oborci by several members of the Serb community, led by Nenad Svemir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us who manned these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were manned by people from Donji Vakuf, local residents, who had been mobilised into one of the units that existed at the time. I didn't know which particular unit, but I knew that it was commanded by an officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you said they were manned by people from Donji Vakuf. Were they manned by Serbs, by Muslims, by Croats? Whom are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what about Muslims? Did they set up their checkpoints, let's say in Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they never did. They never set up a single checkpoint anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then we have another note. It is 5th of March, and it says, the security situation in the municipality is critical. What were you referring to in this entry?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the things that I've just spoken about, namely the fact that members of one community were arming themselves and preparing for war, and this was clear to everyone, whereas others were standing by watching idly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you are saying that it was clear that one community were arming themselves and preparing for war, arming, what did you or what do you know about the arming of Serbs? Did you ever see that civilians would be armed? And I'm referring to the year 1991, beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had already heard, in 1991, and 1992, that Serbs were arming themselves and I even had some information from my own father, who was working at the health centre, that every morning, the drivers who were employed at the health centre were coming back to their pool with dirty vehicles and discussed openly where they had been that day, where they had been carrying weaponry. I also had more information from talking to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And specifically, those Serbs who had been offered to receive weapons on several occasions, and they refused. They didn't want to take any. And they addressed me in my official capacity, asking for my help. My suspicions were confirmed when the bridge was blown up. I think it happened on the 30th of April, when all the Serbs rushed out of their homes wearing civilian clothes but carrying weapons, rifles, some of them even had machine guns. It was then I realised I had been right all along and that the information I had been getting was of good quality, the information concerning such activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to move to the entry under the 2nd of April, 1992, and in English it is page 9, and in B/C/S, it is 0207-2305. It says, under the point 2, political situation, "Request by the SDS to divide institutions, MUP, municipal assembly and bank." Can you make just brief comment to this? Did you know or did you -- were you aware of a division of power, division of MUP, banks and other institutions?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware of such things. They were discussed openly and publicly. However, about this date, it's -- when they insisted that the distribution begin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then you made a comment, "Formation of mono-ethnic JNA unit."

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you make a comment on this entry?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was clear to everyone in Donji Vakuf, abundantly clear. Many Serbs were strutting around in streets carrying weapons, wearing uniforms. We knew roughly who was in which unit. Everybody could see this with their own eyes, everybody was aware of those mono-ethnic units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And just to confirm, mono-ethnic JNA units, are you referring to Serbs, Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And under D, construction of the bridge on the Vrbas River, can you -- can you tell us which bridge you were referring to in this note?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bridge over the Vrbas River, upstream from the city of Donji Vakuf. It was a makeshift bridge, intended only for pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown again the map so he can assist the Judges where the bridge was supposed to be built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of building this bridge?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of building this bridge was to enable in a potential untoward situation, to enable the Serbs who lived in the villages of Brezicani and other neighbouring hamlets, to come to Donji Vakuf, without having to pass through Muslim-inhabited locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And can you show on the map where were these Serb hamlets and villages and these Muslim hamlets and villages which they wanted to avoid?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Cehajici is a predominantly Muslim village, as is the Karici village, but these two villages are not located on this route, on this communication. Then there is the village of Brezicani, which is an exclusively Serb village and a number of other hamlets situated around Brezicani, such as Fonjge, Petkovici and others.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please mark the place where this bridge was supposed to be built with B?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you asking him to mark on the same map that has been written upon by --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on this map, if he would be so kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, the same one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The same one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. He has already marked an X on that map, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, it is location of the Daljan barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what we will do, sir, is we'll go through the same procedure. You will put a mark now as a B, B, and then next to, please, make or put your initials, like last time, like yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was this bridge constructed?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And just to clarify, that it was the proposal of the Serb part to build this bridge or the Muslim part?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This bridge was built by local Serbs. It was built in a record time. They worked even during the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to start slightly different subject, just because we have here your diary, and I would like you to go to the page 8, and in B/C/S, it is the previous page, because I cannot see the ERN number at the top. There is a mark on the left-hand side, handwritten mark, 25. Is it correct? Can you see it? And it starts, "The reserve strength of the Daljan war unit was mobilised on 28 and 29 March." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before I go to your notes, I would like to ask you a few questions about the mobilisation. When mobilisation started in the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I had, the mobilisation started in late March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And normally, who would carry out the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation of reserve units that we had in Donji Vakuf was normally carried out in accordance with the relevant statutory provisions by the National Defence Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the TO, how was the TO involved in mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the mobilisation of personnel, the National Defence Secretariat was only in charge of informing every individual member of a reserve unit of its obligation to report to the assembly point, where we, from the Territorial Defence staff waited and took over these people with whom we then continued working as required.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In your diary, it says, "The reserve strength of the Doljan war unit was called up using their own messenger service, with a third copy of call-up papers which were being kept by this war unit. I have no objections to this type of mobilisation that need to be reviewed here. However, mobilisation of the war unit that was formed in the municipality area is not regular and represents a gross impairment of interethnic relations in Donji Vakuf Municipality area. The mobilisation was not conducted by the competent National Defence Council organ which is operating on behalf -- I'm sorry, or military territorial district organ which is operating on behalf of the JNA. Can you make a comment on this? What did you observe in Donji Vakuf in respect to the mobilisations?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote here that a mobilisation of a small reserve unit had been carried out, whose assembly area was in Daljan barracks. It was under the command of the administrator of the Daljan barracks and I had nothing to do with this particular unit. However, the mobilisation of a war unit of the 19th Brigade, which was being established in the territory of the municipality and whose strength was higher than the municipal TO staff or this Daljani unit, is mentioned here. I made note of that here in my records. And this is just one of the reports that was sent to the district TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So who mobilised this unit? You say that it wasn't conducted according to rules. So who conducted this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular mobilisation was carried out by SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And who did they call up? Were call-up papers distributed to all nationalities living in the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only Serbs were called up and only Serbs responded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were also responsible, you as the commander of the TO, you were responsible for training of reserve units. At that time, did any trainings took place?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The municipal TO did not organise any trainings but I know that this Serb personnel that was called up was trained by JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And how did you learn this information?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the conversations that I had with these people. It was not a secret. An entire village, the village of Kutanja where two of my employees lived, went to the area of Ravna Gradina where training took place, not one training but several trainings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And when you are referring to two of your employees, were they Serbs or were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did they tell you what went on?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of my employees told me this. He said that he had been called up too but that he was not ready to go to participate in this training, or rather that he was not willing to take part in this training, and interestingly, he asked me to make him part of the unit which was located in Daljan barracks, if he had to take up weapons, which is what I did, pursuant to his request. I asked Darko Savic to do that and he made him a member of his group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You also mentioned a second ago this 19th Brigade. When this brigade was formed and who formed it?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, this brigade was established as early as the end of March. All of the units had been established by that time. I know that these units were established by JNA members who had been sent from Banja Luka with this specific assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was it -- was it normal to form this unit or what would be normal procedure, if it wasn't normal?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was by no means a normal procedure. This unit, in a document entitled, "Plan on mobilisational developments," was not envisaged in the area of Donji Vakuf municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What would be normal procedure?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with normal procedures, the ministry, that is the National Defence Secretariat, must receive an order to perform a mobilisation, and a municipal staff has to receive an order from the district or the republican staff, an order to carry out a mobilisation, after which we have to carry out this mobilisation of the reserve force units which would then have to be made part of the Donji Vakuf municipal TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will return back to your diary, and it says, on the bottom of page 8, of English version, I'm not quite sure whether you would be able to see it properly in this version, but it says, "The mobilisation was carried out in secret and members of just one ethnic group were called up." Can you make a brief comment on this?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The call-up was secret. It was partly concealed. The messengers were Serbs only and Serbs only were being called up.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And your comment continues on the following page, in English version, "I feel such behaviour by the JNA to be extremely incorrect because, as the commander of this formation said, that one ethnic group requested the protection of the JNA, so I wonder what would happen if Muslims requested protection. Would the JNA call up only Muslims?" So again just a brief comment on this. Were Muslims called up for the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the last comment is, "Another problem that occurred with the mobilisation of this formation is that a number of the Muslim -- of the municipality TO members are in these units." Are you here again referring to the formation of the 19th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is part of the personnel, that is 60 per cent of personnel, from the TO units, who were members of the 19th Brigade, practically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of this 19th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He introduced himself as a Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Kostic. Later I heard that he was an ex-JNA officer who had retired but was reactivated in the JNA pursuant to a SDS request.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the SDA and Muslim population to this situation, to this mobilisation, and to this situation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot describe this, because people were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you ever try to obtain weapons for Muslim population to -- for their own protection?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Following the mobilisation and the development of the situation, were there other meetings, other negotiations between the SDA members and SDS, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were talks on several occasions. The agenda was similar. It concerned mainly establishment of joint checkpoints, which would have been manned by -- both by members of -- which would have been manned by members of the Bosniak ethnicity as well, that the police should finally disarm people who walked around the streets intoxicated and often opened fire from the rifles they carried around. But this was all to no avail.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In your diary, you also mention, it's somewhere at the beginning, that there were paramilitary formations. This entry appears for the time, for the period of 1991 -- end of 1991, beginning of 1992. Whom do you refer as paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring mainly to people who were wearing civilian clothes but were armed to the hilt, and who stood guard on the access roads to neighbouring villages. After night fall, it was no longer possible for anyone to enter the villages inhabited by Serbs. As far as I'm concerned, they were members of paramilitary formations, because they had their own commanders, and were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you know any of these commanders? Do you know any names?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every single village had its own commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And here you said that there were paramilitary formations in Serb villages, are you aware of any paramilitary formations which would be manned by Muslims or Croats on the territory of the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I heard, and was also able to see, in my local commune, Muslims too stood guard outside their houses, their buildings, in the streets, but were not armed because they didn't have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And in villages, Muslim villages, these people, did they have some weapons?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Often they had military weapons, but some had hunting weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you say they had military weapons. How did they obtain these weapons?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the end, I was able to conclude that the weapons had come from the army. I know that the SDS distributed weapons, and it was only the army and the Territorial Defence reserve force that had weapons, military weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: But I asked you about Muslim villages, and you said that there were military weapons, so I'm asking how these Muslim obtained these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 14972 to 14976. military weapons.

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I said that Muslims stood guard, but were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And if there were any guards in Muslim villages, did they have any type of weapons, hunting, military, pistols, just any kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had weapons didn't dare to carry it because it would have been confiscated, and they would have been arrested and taken to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show you some more documents. Do you want to have a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After the break, I will have 30 more minutes, just go through the documents, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask for your cooperation and have a very short break? I suggest ten minutes only.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour I really don't think that's possible. We have no facilities on this floor any more so I have to go some distance. I assume my client has the same problem, plus I need to talk with him so I'd really ask for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 20 minutes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I am done with the diary and I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1711.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This document is dated 14th of April, 1992. These are minutes of the second session of the assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, held on 14 of April, 1992. 14th of April, 1992, is also the day when you stopped working, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In this -- in these minutes, it says, Zoran Glisic said that he had pointed out that the council for National Defence was not competent to decide on -- probably -- division and that the SDA and SDS should be in charge of this issue. In your diary, there was an entry for 14 of April as well, and you continued discussing the situation in Donji Vakuf. Do you remember whether -- or do you recall whether the higher SDS leaders were going to Banja Luka to conduct some meetings or whatever?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember they did go to Banja Luka, but I don't know whether they went there for meetings or possibly discussions and negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And when we are talking about higher SDS leaders, who are these -- or who were these people? Do you know any names?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I know that Nedjeljko Ninkovic, Gojko Ninkovic, Zagorac, Nikica Zagorac and some other people took the most prominent part in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know the name Nikola Kisin?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He too was one of the leaders of the Donji Vakuf SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And these minutes go on page 3, like on the page 3 of English version, in B/C/S version it is the second page, when it says, "Gojko Ninkovic said that our citizens had been mobilised to the TO, which was growing into the JNA. The mobilisation of the entire population and the preparation of the territory are on the way." Can you make just very brief comment on this entry?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoken about this. It means that the SDS was making intensive preparations in that territory, conducting the distribution of weapons and ultimately mobilised men into its own units, setting up these units, and this is probably the conclusion of all the activities that had taken place beforehand, and he's probably just taking note of this fact at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I will read another of his comments: "We shall have as much territory as we are organised and prepared to defend." On the page 5 of English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Madam Richterova, please before you move away from this, can you clarify, was the name of gentleman you mentioned Ninkovic, Gojko or Nedjeljko, if the witness can assist us? Nedjeljko or Gojko? You said Gojko but I think it was Nedjeljko? Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gojko, G-O-J-K-O, we are talking about two brothers, Gojko and Nedjeljko. Gojko was in charge of conducting these activities while Nedjeljko was I believe president of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So both brothers were engaged in politics, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is the last page in B/C/S, under the point 4, it says, the assembly adopted a decision on establishing a Serbian SJB, in the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, Rajko Kisin was appointed SJB chief, Jovo Satara was appointed SJB commander and Zoran Ilic, deputy commander. Is it correct? Do you remember that there would be a division of the SJB?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have just one question. There was this secretary of the municipal secretariat for people's defence. Do you happen to know who was -- who held this position?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretary of the National Defence Secretariat was Mile Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this Zoran Ilic, deputy commander, was he a relative to Mile Ilic, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know. I don't know whether the two were related.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the following point, 6, it says, "Miodrag Jandric said that at its session held on 11 April, 1992, the Assembly of the Serbian People of Autonomous Region of Krajina had adopted a decision on establishing the SDK and that we had to decide how we should deal with this issue in the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf." Do you know whether the SDK was separated and joined Banja Luka SDK?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in this period, not all the documentation had been completed about the dissociation of their SDK. It was probably done later but I'm not aware of the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The next point is 7, "The assembly unanimously decided that all paramilitary formations in the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf should be disarmed and placed under the single command of the JNA." Do you know what they are referring to? Which paramilitary formations are here mentioning?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is meant here are the formations which had already been established in this period, and it was clear that they were under nobody's control. Along roads they stopped private vehicles, buses, and they robbed people, including some Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were they put under the command of JNA?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not while I was in Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1715 and 1718. Let's start with 1715. This document is dated 29 April, 1992, and I only have slight problem because it says further that at its session on 14th May, 1992, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Donji Vakuf adopted the following decision, decision on the change of organisational link, and it says SDK Donji Vakuf branch, join an organisational link up with the social accountancy service of Banja Luka, and it withdraw from the regional Bugojno branch office. Do you know whether it happened in April or in May?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, Madam Richterova, is the document that I see on the ELMO your document, Prosecution's document, or is it the registry's?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This is a copy and here I was informed that there was a marking but it was marking on English. I can immediately replace it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the future, try to avoid handing documents which are marked or highlighted or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can immediately replace it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not exactly something serious but just for the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem, Madam Richterova, I know it was done inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The other document is 14 -- date 14 May, 1992 and it's Exhibit 1718.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And a decision to end payments between the Donji Vakuf SDK, local branch and to Bugojno SDK regional branch and redirect them to the Banja Luka regional branch. What I am interested in in this document is Crisis Staff. This document says, the title of this document, is, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Donji Vakuf Municipality Crisis Staff." Do you know at the time you were in Donji Vakuf, was Crisis Staff established?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was. But this Crisis Staff was a joint one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this joint Crisis Staff, when was it established?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in January, towards the beginning of the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You have January or towards the beginning of the year, and which year are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And who were the members of this joint Crisis Staff? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who the members were but I know that the SDS and the SDA had the most seats in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of that Crisis Staff, which was established either in January or towards the -- towards the beginning of the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the Crisis Staff was to deal with all specific situations and incidents that could arise in the territory of Donji Vakuf municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know how long this initial Crisis Staff functioned?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know whether at some point there was another Crisis Staff which would be manned only representatives of one ethnicity? Ethnicities, either Muslims --

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You don't know. You don't know whether in April or May there was a Crisis Staff, either Muslim or Serb?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P888? It is in the binder. It is dated 19 April, 1992. If you take it in chronological order. I apologise because these two SDK documents were taken out of order. So if you go -- it is right behind 1713 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And on the first page, we can read, "The 19" -- I will start from the title. It's document of the 30th Partisan division command, and the date is 19 of April, 1992. And in the middle of the page, it says, "19th Partisan Brigade will conduct additional mobilisation in the municipalities of Kupres, Bugojno and Donji Vakuf, with the mobilised forces" just the first sentence. This 19th Partisan Brigade, is the same Brigade you were referring to in your previous testimony? This 19th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to show the witness Exhibit P629. In English, I'm referring to the bottom part of the page number 1. It's under point 3, situation on the ground. In B/C/S language, it is on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And it says, "Caution, fear and uncertainty are still present among the population of all nationalities. It is particularly prominent in the crisis municipalities such as Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, and among them is also Donji Vakuf." This document is document which was issued by 5th Corps command and the date is 2nd of May, 1992. It is to the 2nd Military District command. 2nd May, 1992, it is the time after the destruction of the bridge over the Vrbas River. Can you just briefly describe the atmosphere in the Donji Vakuf town and in the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, when the bridge was blown up, I was visiting my father, and when it happened, I ran to my apartment, and on the way, I ran into Nedjeljko Ninkovic. He asked me to walk with him and that's how we got to the residential buildings in Donji Vakuf. Perhaps some ten minutes after the explosion. We watched together as both Serbs and Bosniaks came out of their buildings. However, the Serbs were carrying rifles, whereas Bosniaks had no weapons. Nedjeljko Ninkovic seemed very embarrassed and he raised the racket, yelling at Serbs, "Why have you come out with your weapons? There is no war going on." After this, I went to the place where the bridge used to be, and I saw the ruins of the bridge and the surrounding structures. Some of them were totally destroyed, 100 per cent destroyed, and others were partially damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment, because we would have -- needed to clarify this later on in any case. There has been throughout the testimony of this witness today in particular various references to a bridge. He marked on the map 16 -- I can't remember the exact number, and with a D -- with a B, the bridge that he was referring to at the time, which I understand was the makeshift bridge for pedestrians only that was built in a very short time by the Serbs to enable them to reach Donji Vakuf without having to pass through Muslim villages. This is not the same bridge that was blown up on the 30th of April allegedly by Croats, no? It's a different bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The bridge which was blown up on the 30th of April, was it rebuilt, reconstructed, repaired or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Immediately after the explosion, some two days later, the engineering units of the JNA started putting up a prefab bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our apologies to you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to make it absolutely clear I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1760.26 -- no marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If you could have a look at this picture and tell us what we can see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken after the war. This is the new bridge that was built in the same place where the bridge that had been blown up on the 30th of April, 1992, used to stand. In the background, behind the bridge, on the right-hand side, you can see one house that was in the process of construction and that was totally destroyed, and another house that was also totally destroyed during the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with this picture and I would like to show the witness Exhibit 631. This is again a military document, 5th Corps command, dated 12th of May, 1992. I am referring to the point 3, situation in the ground, which is in both cases in both languages on the first page, and in B/C/S it goes to the second page. And it says, "The Muslim and Croat population is moving out of the area of Donji Vakuf towards Bugojno." Can you tell us what made these people leaving the Donji Vakuf municipality or the Donji Vakuf town?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, briefly, the reason was the fear reigning in Donji Vakuf. If you want to elaborate on this, I can corroborate this with some facts that have to do with what the people of Muslim ethnicity in Donji Vakuf experienced at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, please. What they were afraid of?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arming of the Serbs had begun and it was no secret in Donji Vakuf. The mobilisation had been carried out. Many people had heard by that time about the establishment of the Serbian Municipality of Donji Vakuf, and they understood what this meant. Furthermore, there were paramilitary formations, in other words armed men who were going around looting, shooting, and intimidating the population. Then came the explosion of the bridge, and the radio announcement in April saying that all the people should turn over their weapons to the Serbian police station or at the barracks, the military barracks. Everybody realised then that searches would be carried out by the military police of the JNA or by the Serbian police that had been established in the administrative building of Konar --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the building.

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This radio announcement was the last drop that caused unrest among the non-Serb population of Donji Vakuf and put them on edge. And as a result, they stampeded out of Donji Vakuf on the 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What these people took with them? Were they able to take what they needed, what they wanted?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trust me, it was a sorry scene. Women were crying. Most of them carried only one plastic bag in their hands containing the bear necessities, and they had to walk 12 kilometres to Bugojno in order to save their necks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know approximately how many people left during this period of time, the Donji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that by the -- by the 11th of May, 1992, 95 per cent of the population, Muslim and Croat population, had left Donji Vakuf, at least 95 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with this document. I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1764, and in your binders, it is the very last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will it be the very last question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is the last sentence of this military document, dated 13 of May, 1992. It says, "Government representatives of the Muslim ethnicity have left government organs in Donji Vakuf municipality so that authority is now mainly being exercised by representatives of the Serbian people." Were the authority exercised by the Serbian municipality just from 13 of May or did they exercise the authority also before?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear from the documents that we saw previously that they had their organs of government with no Muslims. As far as I remember, joint bodies stopped functioning as early as March or April. So this military report seems strange. I mean, I wonder how come it -- they didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show the witness Exhibit P51. It is a document dated 14 May, 1992. It is a meeting with presidents of municipalities in the zone of responsibility of the division. On the first page, it says that the commander of the 30th Partisan division was Colonel Stanislav Galic. Did you know at that time that 30th Partisan Division under the command of Colonel Stanislav Galic was operating in that area?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was the 19th Brigade attached to the 30th Partisan Division, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: On the following page, you will see Donji Vakuf SO. It says, among others, "Reinforcement is on the way of the 19th Partisan Brigades" and then it goes on, "Part of our forces is controlling the zone towards Jajce and Torlakovac" most probably "while the other part is controlling the zone towards Bugojno, the brigade's biggest problem being the village Prusac where a large number of green berets are concentrated." So my question is were green berets in the village of Prusac or I will start with my question: Who lived in the village of Prusac, people of which ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority population in Prusac was Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were there a large number of green berets?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no green berets there at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1722.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It says press corps it's dated 29 May, 1992, and the last two sentences says or three sentences, "The situation in Donji Vakuf is rather serious. Gangs of HOS members and green berets are terrorising and looting in the town, and the number of snipers lying in wait in houses increases in night fall." As I said it is a press release or press corps dated 29 May, 1992, the situation described is in this document, is it accurate reflection of the situation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that the Bosniak population, with the exception of the sick and the elderly who had remained in Donji Vakuf, left Donji Vakuf and went to Bugojno and a small part to Travnik, on the 8th, the 9th, the 10th and the 11th. Therefore I'm unable to comment on this. This is simply impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit P950.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is document, military document, 1st Krajina Corps command, 3rd June, 1992, and it says, "The 30th infantry division continues to mop up the Vrbas River valley in the villages of Vinac and Torlakovac." Who lived in the villages of Vinac and Torlakovac, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Vinac. I do not wish to comment because it belongs to the Jajce municipality. As for the village of Torlakovac, all residents were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Have you heard the term of "mop up"?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What does it mean, or how do you understand the term?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what "mop up" meant during this period. I had opportunity to hear about it. It was just a Serb formation that went around Muslim villages, opened fire from rifles and automatic weapons. Its members entered villages to check who remained behind. I know, for instance, that the village of Doganovci located in the immediate vicinity of Torlakovac, that this is what happened. I know about this particular village because I was born there. All those who remained in the village were either murdered or arrested. Many houses were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And do you know whether, in either of these villages, there was any armed resistance?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no armed resistance in the village of Torlakovac. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness Exhibit 1729.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This is another military document, combat report, dated 21st June, 1992, command of the 19th Partisan Brigade, and it says, "Except for sporadic provoking shots fired at 8.30 hours at Bribraca from the direction of the school in Prusac, there were no other serious enemy activities." It goes on like, "Grouping of men was noticed during the day in Prusac." It goes on, "It was decided to reconnoitre and explore the area of Kisinov Potok with a view to taking more concrete measures and destroying the above-mentioned group, as well as intimidating and dispersing the men in Prusac." And the document continues talking about Prusac, in June 1992 what was the situation in Prusac? Was there resistance, armed resistance?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were armed civilians in Prusac. They had between 10 and 15 hunting rifles. I think they had several automatic rifles as well. I know that they had very little ammunition for these weapons. During that period, they still didn't have a front line around the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can I show the witness Exhibit 1754?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope we don't have to stay the rest of the sitting listening to the security radio messages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This is a report on the work of the Donji Vakuf public security station between the 1st April, 1992, and 25th December, 1992, and it describes the situation from February 1992, high ranking Serbian personnel have directed the efforts towards the preparation for the separation and setting up a Serbian public security, and as a result, a Serbian public security station was established in mid-April. Do you remember when the SGB -- SJB was separated and did Serb policemen wear different uniforms than the Muslim or non-Serb policemen?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I no longer remember the date, though I was aware of it at the time. I remember the events taking place at the time. The Serb police became separate, and went -- and when they moved to the administration building of the Komar company. I also know that Serb police officers signed up for some different uniforms, slightly different uniforms, than the regular ones. And I also know that highly capable young men of Serb ethnicity from Donji Vakuf were elected and became members of the police, of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When we are talking about these new uniforms, Serb police, I would ask you at any point did to Donji Vakuf arrive some military unit from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a special unit, at least this is how Serbs who still communicated with me at the time referred to it. Me and my colleague from the municipal staff were taken to the Daljan barracks on several occasions by this special unit. They wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And thank you for that information and I will go back to this document. It says in -- it is in the second paragraph, "There was a need at the time to set up a collection centre for Croatian and Muslim men and we dealt with everything concerning their detentions and investigation together with the military security." Do you know any collection centres which were set up in Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you name some for us?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, for instance, that there was a collection centre in a TO warehouse. I know that some of my neighbours were detained in the Vrbaspromet company warehouse. I also know that my relatives from Oborci were detained in the Slav restaurant in Oborci. Then I know that some people were taken to Semisnica motel located outside the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have the last document. It's Exhibit 1757. It is a document issued by Ministry of the Interior, Banja Luka security service centre, public security centre, Srbobran, dated 4th of October, 1993, and it's chronological factual report on the setting up of a Serbian SJB and police participation in the war. I would refer you to the second page, which starts, "We will just mention some of the more significant operations in which the police participated. We have the first one, on 21st May, 1992, the operation to liberate Korenici village. Korenici village, who lived in this village? People of which ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People of Muslim ethnicity, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And were they needed to be liberated?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, by whom? From whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I am asking you, because it says the operation to liberate Korenici village. So what do you think they were -- what this document is referring to?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, when this was discussed, reference was to the cleansing of the village, and the deportation of its residents, which was followed by plunder and arson. This is what was meant by a liberated Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It also says a little bit further, "There was no great resistance by the Muslim extremists but they succeeded in escaping to the territory." Were you aware of any Muslim extremists, either in this village or on the territory of the Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for sure that in Korenici there remained several old and sick people who couldn't or wouldn't join other residents. However, after this action, some of them managed to arrive in Bugojno. Others, however, have not been heard of ever since. We don't know whether they are alive or dead. But at any rate, after this action, there were no Muslims left in Korenici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then they are referring to the operation in Torlakovac on the 3rd of June and we already saw military documents talking about the mopping up operations in this village. Then Doganovci, if I'm not mistaken it is a village in the vicinity of Torlakovac, I think you mentioned. I didn't get it in the transcript. This village of Doganovci, who lived there?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims only.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And was there any resistance?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was none.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then we have operation on 11 July, for you it is on the page 3 in B/C/S, and operation was carried out, together with VRS over a large area of the Oborci and Seher villages, significant territory was captured and with this act enemy disappeared from Donji Vakuf-Turbe area. Who lived in Oborci and Seher villages?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority populations in Oborci and Seher was Muslims but there were some Serbs as well, a small number of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Is it correct what is stated in this document, that enemy disappeared so -- were there any remaining Muslims living in Oborci and Seher after this operation?

utterances.speaker: SENAD ALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before this operation, if you will allow me, in these two villages, which are virtually connected, both Serbs and a number of Muslims lived. The Muslims that had not yet fled. Military vehicles would normally and without problems pass through these villages carrying soldiers and officers in the direction of Jariciste where they were being trained. There were no problems whatsoever for Serbs or the military there because they were already present in these villages. During this period of time, in the village of Oborci, or to be more precise, between Oborci and this other village, my parents were staying, and according to what they said, all Muslims remained in their houses during the day, and during the night they would go to the woods because nights were very dangerous. My father and my mother, together with other Muslims, finally left this village sometime before this action took place, and went to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We have another entry, 17 August, 1992, operation to liberate Prusac village, which says that it was the largest Ustasha stronghold. When we were talking about Prusac in June, you said there wasn't still a combat zone. In August, did the situation change?
